correctness.rationale: For arbitrary positive part sizes and any nonnegative palette size, each color class is threshold exactly when at most one original part has multiplicity greater than one, since two heavy parts force an induced four-cycle, whereas zero or one heavy part allows a universal-vertex/isolated-vertex construction. This equivalence gives the disjoint labelled-class EGF terms; multiplication over named colors and coefficient extraction yields the exact count. Inclusion-exclusion gives onto and unordered refinements. Pigeonhole lower bound on large parts and an explicit constructive allocation prove the minimum formula. The included independent literal induced-graph/EGF checker verified 166 instances and 345279 assignments; finite checks are supplemental only.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact all-palette labelled counting series, onto counts and unordered class counts on arbitrary complete multipartite graphs; the sharp size threshold is included as a structural corollary, not as a new general decision algorithm. The primary 2026 work proves hardness and threshold correspondence without these formulas. Earlier 2005/2012 work gives polynomial decision algorithms for the larger class of cographs, which already covers computability of the minimum but does not logically yield the exact distribution of all labelled colorings. The open 2006 PDF treats approximation and a different edge-degree threshold. A targeted mathematical-record search and exact phrase/alias searches found no enumerator; this is qualified priority evidence, not a uniqueness certificate.

No independent historical-priority adjudication has been performed.

value.rationale: The theorem counts every named-palette and every nonempty unordered threshold-induced partition of an unrestricted complete multipartite family, directly motivated by the 2026 alternating coloring hardness problem and classical split-coloring. It furnishes an exact multivariate distribution and a universal part-size transition, not an arbitrary slice or one finite table. Prior cograph decision algorithms do not supply this full labeled solution-space enumeration. The theorem makes no claim about general graphs, and acknowledges incomplete historical access.
